what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted by roll call to recommend Rob Thompson for the part-time recreation director job, sending it to the Select Board; the count was apparently 3-1.
The vote followed a long, heated exchange on how the commission, the DPW and the director should work together.
The commission will hold a separate workshop early in the new year on roles and communication among the commission, town manager, DPW and director.
Discussion of field-use fees was deferred to June, so any change would take effect later than the coming season.
The chair will ask the Marshall Park consultant to present two concept designs by Zoom around January 20.

why_it_matters: The recreation director runs programs and fields that residents and youth leagues use, and the Select Board now takes up whether the post becomes permanent.
Field-use fees will not change for the 2022 season, because leagues have already opened sign-ups, so any change comes later and would be set after that June discussion.
Portable toilets for next summer, Marshall Park's design and a youth league's unpaid 2021 fees all point to spending from town and revolving-fund money that the commission has yet to settle.
watch_next: Select Board consideration of the Thompson recommendation.
Marshall Park concept designs presented by Zoom around January 20, and the portable toilet contract reopened by late February.

meetings.headline: Parks Commission chose Wolla to design the Marshall Park overhaul and authorized skatepark land for preliminary design.
meetings.summary: The Parks Commission voted to grant the Lunenburg Skatepark project space at Marshall Park (up to 8,000 sq ft) to proceed with a preliminary design, after lengthy discussion of siting, parking, maintenance costs, and fundraising progress. It also voted to hire Wolla as the landscape architecture/engineering firm for the broader Marshall Park redesign, over three competing firms, and set December 2nd as the next meeting, doubling as a public forum on the park's future.

public_comment.topic: youth soccer season winding down; asked whether play could continue with portable nets after town nets are locked up for winter

votes.motion: Grant space to the Lunenburg Skatepark project, up to 8,000 square feet, at the location shown in the plans presented, for the purpose of the group creating a preliminary design
Accept the proposal from Wolla for architectural and landscape engineering services for the Marshall Park project

budget_items.what_was_said: Open Space Committee received a donation from a farm operation that relocated instead of building behind Walmart, usable at the committee's discretion; Parks was asked to consider proposing a project (e.g. town beach weed removal or Northfield Park signage) for some of that money.

The skatepark group reported roughly $130,000 raised in cash and in-kind donations, with a further $10,000 and $25,000 pledged for December and January; estimated construction cost was given per square foot for the 8,000 sq ft park, with an estimated $25,000-$40,000 still needed before breaking ground.

minutes.summary: The Parks Commission voted to grant the Lunenburg Skatepark project space at Marshall Park (up to 8,000 sq ft) to proceed with a preliminary design, after lengthy discussion of siting, parking, maintenance costs, and fundraising progress. It also voted to hire Wolla as the landscape architecture/engineering firm for the broader Marshall Park redesign, over three competing firms, and set December 2nd as the next meeting, doubling as a public forum on the park's future.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to let the Lunenburg Skatepark project use a defined area of Marshall Park to develop a preliminary design.
It also voted to hire Wolla as the landscape architecture and engineering firm for the full Marshall Park redesign, chosen over three competing firms.
The skatepark group reported fundraising progress but said an amount was still needed before construction could start.
The next meeting, December 2nd, was set to double as a public forum on the Marshall Park redesign with the design firm.
Commissioners were asked to propose how to spend an Open Space Committee donation ahead of a December meeting of that committee.

why_it_matters: Marshall Park's redesign now has a hired design firm and a defined skatepark footprint, moving the project from concept toward a plan residents will see at the December forum.

The skatepark's construction is expected to be funded by the group's own fundraising rather than town appropriation, so how much it still needs to raise affects whether the project breaks ground on the timeline discussed.
A separate donation held by the Open Space Committee is still unassigned, and the Parks Commission may propose a project for part of it before that committee's December meeting.
